title: Terraform-driven healing controller and stepwise runbook for persistent VPC probe degradations
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Scope: Build a small controller/operator that orchestrates safe, minimal Terraform-based repairs for common persistent VPC health-check failures and produce an operator-friendly runbook for on-call. This ticket covers the design, a reference implementation (opensourced internally), CI tests that run terraform plan/apply in a sandbox, and a validated runbook that SREs and Solutions Eng can follow. Goal is to close frequent incidents where probes repeatedly fail due to single-instance drift (route table detachment, iptables rules, SG misconfiguration) without a full manual IaC lifecycle intervention. Excludes large-scale network re-architecting or customer-facing UI changes.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Controller can detect a set of configurable probe-failure patterns from monitoring (CloudWatch/Prometheus) and map to a named remediation plan
A2: Controller executes a scoped Terraform plan that is limited to a single module/target and runs in a dry-run by default unless an explicit auto-approve policy is enabled
A3: Runbook exists with step-by-step manual remediation for each mapped pattern, plus escalation matrix and playbook for rolling back operator changes
A4: CI pipeline includes a mock VPC environment (or k8s-based simulator) where terraform plans are validated and drift detection tests pass
A5: Safety gates (rate limits, approval windows, canary checks) are implemented and documented
A6: On-call runbook tested in two simulated incidents and postmortems captured as linked artifacts
runbook_steps: 1) Triage: Confirm probe type (AGENT_HEALTH, NODE_TCP_PROBE, ROUTE_CHECK) and time window in Redwood Console alerts
2) Scope: Query node IDs and affected subnets; identify last IaC apply via terraform state metadata in S3/GCS
3) Manual quick-fix: If change is simple (security group missing rule), run documented terraform apply against specific target with --target flag and comment on PR/incident

4) Operator path: If recurring or >2 incidents in 24h, trigger the healing-controller with a tagged remediation plan (see automated_remediation_design) in dry-run mode, review the plan in Slack thread, then approve
5) Post-apply validation: Run probe test suite and verify traffic flows (connectivity, kv-cache priming) for 10 minutes, then mark incident as mitigated
6) Rollback: If any downstream errors occur within 15 minutes, run the stored terraform rollback plan and notify stakeholders
7) Postmortem: Attach plan, apply logs, diff of state and follow-up action items to incident ticket
automated_remediation_design: A lightweight controller (golang) subscribes to alert streams and scales a remediation worker. It maps alert signatures to a remediation recipe that contains: terraform module target(s), pre-check script, post-check script, allowed drift tolerances, and a safety policy. Controller always runs terraform plan first and posts the plan to a designated Slack channel + incident thread. Auto-apply is disabled by default; enabling requires a RUBRIC (team + time window) and a stored approval token. Controller supports two run modes: dry-run and apply-with-approval. All terraform ops run inside ephemeral build runners with read-only access to remote state snapshots; when apply is required we ensure state lock via backend and make minimal change sets using --target where possible. Remediation recipes are versioned and stored alongside IaC in the private-deploy-ops repo.
safety_guards: Only allow terraform --target of single resource group in automated mode
Require state lock and snapshotting before any apply
Rate limit: max 1 automated remediation per project per 30 minutes
Approval token required for any cross-subnet or route-table changes
Circuit breaker: if post-check fails twice, stop automated applies and escalate to on-call
Audit logs: all plan/apply output archived to S3 and linked in incident
testing_plan: Unit tests for mapping logic (alert -> remediation recipe)
Integration tests using localkube or kinD to simulate node-level failures and assert controller applies correct --target plan
End-to-end tests in a sandbox account that run plan -> apply -> validation scripts (no auto-approve)
Load test: simulate 100 concurrent probe failures to validate rate-limiting and queueing behavior
Safety test: Force failure in post-check to ensure rollback path and circuit breaker trigger
rollout_plan: 1) Merge design and reference implementation behind feature flag in private-deploy-ops
2) Deploy controller to staging (non-production) cluster and run scheduled remediation drills
3) Invite SRE + Solutions Eng to trial for 2 weeks in low-risk customers (internal infra and one pilot customer)
4) Open a temporary manual approval channel; do not enable auto-apply for production customers until metrics meet thresholds
5) After 2 successful drills and approval from Security, enable auto-apply selectively and monitor for 72h
6) Gradual ramp to full production for all Private deployments with telemetry dashboards and alerting for failed remediations
